charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For HUTCHMED (China) Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For HUTCHMED (China) Limited: most of this balance is short-term investments rather than pure cash -- $1,296m of the $1,367m shown at FY2025 -- built up from the FY2023 Takeda upfront and the FY2025 SHPL divestment proceeds; debt is small relative to the cash pile.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For HUTCHMED (China) Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For HUTCHMED (China) Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For HUTCHMED (China) Limited: FY2025 net income ($456.9m) was dominated by a one-off ~$415.8m net gain on divesting a 45% stake in the Shanghai Hutchison Pharmaceuticals JV -- a cash receipt, but not a repeatable operating result, so compare it against FCF rather than taking net income at face value.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF
  • One-off divestment/disposal gains inflating a single year's net income

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For HUTCHMED (China) Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For HUTCHMED (China) Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For HUTCHMED (China) Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For HUTCHMED (China) Limited: this line blends in-China product sales, the Other Ventures distribution business, and lumpy licensing/milestone income from ex-China partners -- FY2023's jump and FY2024's pullback are mostly the Takeda upfront, not underlying demand. See the Licensing/Royalty chart below for the split.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

licensingRoyalty.title: Licensing/milestone revenue vs royalties
licensingRoyalty.content:
Licensing & milestones is upfront and regulatory-milestone payments from out-licensing deals (Takeda for FRUZAQLA/fruquintinib ex-China, AstraZeneca for ORPATHYS/savolitinib) -- large but one-off. Royalties is the ongoing percentage of partner sales once a drug is approved and marketed -- smaller per period but recurring and compounding as partnered drugs gain share.

For HUTCHMED: FY2023 revenue ($838m) was inflated by a $279m Takeda milestone that will not repeat; royalties grew from $2.7m (FY2019) to roughly $68-71m/year (FY2024-25) as FRUZAQLA's ex-China launch ramped, which is the more durable read on partner-drug traction.

What to watch:

  • Royalty growth rate as the real signal of ex-China drug uptake
  • New licensing deals (GSK) as the next potential milestone spike
  • Don't extrapolate a milestone year's revenue forward

rnd.title: Research & development expense
rnd.content:
R&D expense is what HUTCHMED spends discovering and clinically developing its oncology/immunology pipeline, shown against revenue.

For HUTCHMED: R&D fell from a peak of $387m (FY2022) to $148m (FY2025) as costly late-stage trials for FRUZAQLA and ORPATHYS completed and partners (Takeda, AstraZeneca) now fund more of the ex-China development -- a shift from self-funded to partner-funded R&D, not simply a pipeline cut.

What to watch:

  • R&D as a share of revenue trending down (operating leverage) vs down because the pipeline is shrinking
  • New clinical-stage assets entering the pipeline to replace what has matured out

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For HUTCHMED (China) Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
